messages:
John D.: Hey team — heads up: our prod org (org_8942) showed ~3k credits at 23:30 PST yesterday and this morning we were at 0 and getting 429s. Customers hit failed responses. Are resets at 00:00 UTC or tenant local midnight? This feels like an early depletion/reset mismatch.

Jen (Support): Sorry you're seeing this, John. We're looking. Quick Qs: did you run any large batch embedding jobs overnight or enable any burst windows? Any screenshots of the billing/usage UI?

John D.: We had a scheduled nightly rerank job (smallish) but nothing that should eat 3k credits. UI showed ~3,120 credits at ~23:40 PST (screenshot attached in ticket). By 04:10 PST the app started returning 429s and the UI showed 0. No plan changes in the org.

Jen (Support): thanks — can you share the request IDs for a failing call? Also, can you run one quick check: curl -I to the API and look for these headers: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining and X-Redwood-Quota-Reset? Example: 

```
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

John D.: here's a failing request id: req_01G9H2XQ4Y. I ran the curl earlier, headers returned `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0` and `X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: 1719187200` (that timestamp is in UTC midnight for their billing anchor?). Not sure.

support-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-8942-credit-drop - assigned to Jen (Support).

Emma (Billing): pinging in — I can see a refill event for org_8942 scheduled at 00:00 UTC monthly anchor, but there is also a manual commit renewal at the enterprise account level that sometimes runs later. I'm checking the ledger.

Rao (Infra): putting infra hats on — possible causes: (a) background refill job lag (queue backlog), (b) streaming token double-counting edge where initial chunk counted twice during a retry, or (c) tenant timezone anchor mismatch when a tenant was migrated between orgs. We'll check job timings and the refill worker logs.

Milo (Dev): also want to check whether quota accounting has any eventual consistency window — we flush counters asynchronously every N minutes. If a burst consumed tokens and UI showed stale count ~23:40, there can be a race. We intentionally let the UI be eventually consistent to avoid DB pressure.

Jen (Support): repro steps for infra/devs — from ticket: 
1) Query ledger: `SELECT * FROM credits_ledger WHERE org_id='org_8942' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;`
2) Check refill worker logs in prod-queues: `kubectl logs deploy/refill-worker -n prod --since=6h | grep org_8942`
3) Inspect API request logs for req_01G9H2XQ4Y: `rg "req_01G9H2XQ4Y" /var/log/redwood/api/*`
4) Validate streaming accounting: tail token-processor logs for request windows 23:30-04:30 PST.

Rao (Infra): found something: refill-worker retried a batch at 00:02 UTC due to transient DB timeout, and the success ack came at 00:03:14 UTC. That means UI and headers could show 0 until the worker actually wrote the ledger. The client saw 429s between 00:00 and 00:03 UTC.

Milo (Dev): thanks — I also see several streaming connections from the org that had two sequential retry fragments during the same user session around 23:58-00:01 UTC. There's a known bug where ephemeral retry increments the token counter twice for the same logical token window if the retry occurs before the dedupe checkpoint. I have a PR to fix it but not deployed to prod.

John D.: so is this a billing bug (we lost credits) or just visible lag and double-counting? Our customers were impacted — what can you do right now?

Emma (Billing): immediate remediation: I issued a manual top-up of 4k credits at 00:20 UTC to cover the outage window so you shouldn't see further 429s. I'll add a zero-dollar adjustment record and we can roll back after root cause. Also enabling threshold webhook for <=5% so you get notified earlier.

Jen (Support): next steps we recommend to customer: 
- I) We temporarily topped you up (Emma confirmed).
- II) If you have critical production workflows, add a 5% buffer in monthly budgeting or set up the webhook for low-credit alerts.
- III) We'll provide a short incident write-up once infra/dev confirm root cause.

Rao (Infra): root cause summary for now: refill worker had a 2-3 minute delay due to transient DB timeouts during midnight UTC boundary; concurrently, a streaming retry bug resulted in some tokens being double-counted for a subset of requests. Combined effect: brief window of perceived depletion and customer-visible 429s.

Milo (Dev): mitigation plan: (1) deploy streaming-token dedupe fix (PR#4821) to prod in 2 business days behind a canary, (2) add an extra in-memory grace window at refill boundary to tolerate 1-2m worker lag, (3) surface `X-Redwood-Quota-Pending-Refill: true` header during refill boundary so clients can distinguish permanent exhaustion vs pending refill.

John D.: appreciate the fast response. Please include exact timestamps of when my org was topped and which requests were double-counted so I can explain to ops staff.

Jen (Support): noted. We'll follow up in the ticket with a timeline: failed request window (00:00-00:03 UTC), manual top-up at 00:20 UTC, refill worker success at 00:03:14 UTC (wrote ledger), and PR/Dep schedule. Expect a post-incident summary later today. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident #INC-2026-8942 updated: status -> investigating -> actioned.

Emma (Billing): audit note: I created adjustment AJ-5589 and enabled org webhook low-credit alert for org_8942.

Milo (Dev): putting the dedupe PR into staging now, adding extra unit tests to cover streaming retry scenarios. I'll post the canary tag once ready.

John D.: thanks everyone. We'll monitor and close the customer ticket once we see stable headers and no 429s.

Jen (Support): closing loop here: please DM if you see any reoccurrence. We'll attach the full timeline and logs to the ticket for your compliance team.
